target_customer: Young and first-time Indonesian retail investors buying mutual funds, then stocks and ETFs
problem: Few Indonesians invested because brokerage access, minimums and financial education were poor. Ajaib offered a simple app to invest in funds and later stocks.
business_model: Retail brokerage and mutual fund distribution with transaction and fund fees

founders.name: Anderson Sumarli
education: Stanford Graduate School of Business, MBA
founders.background_notes: Former BCG consultant and part-time investor per KrASIA, March 2021. Named co-founder and CEO on the YC page.

founders.name: Yada Piyajomkwan
education: Stanford Graduate School of Business, MBA
founders.background_notes: Thai classmate of Sumarli at Stanford, financial consulting background, per KrASIA.

competitors.name: Bareksa
competitors.what: Mutual fund marketplace with financial data, tools and news

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app on top of licensed fund distribution and later broker infrastructure; the hard parts were regulation and integrations, not research.

defensibility.rationale: OJK registration and later broker licence, plus a user base of young investors, but rivals such as Bareksa and Stockbit offered similar products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Ajaib launched its own brokerage, Ajaib Sekuritas, in 2020.

market_need_then: Indonesia had low retail investing penetration and a young population; the company described Robinhood and XP Investimentos as inspiration (KrASIA 2021).

branding.name_origin: Ajaib means wonderful in Indonesian, per KrASIA. Why the founders chose it was not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Educational toward young investors, stated mission of financial education

branding.community_and_virality: Press calls it the Robinhood of Indonesia and the first investment app unicorn in Southeast Asia; no merch or fan community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: A local-language word meaning wonderful that fits the product, and strong press as a unicorn, but no sourced mascot or community assets.

pivots.why: Search results say stock trading came later, with Ajaib Sekuritas launching in June 2020

outcome_analysis: Ajaib began as a mutual fund app, raised a 2.1 million dollar seed in 2019, then added stock brokerage in 2020 as Indonesian retail investing boomed. It raised a Series A in two parts in 2021 and a 153 million dollar Series B at unicorn status in October 2021. It cut 67 staff in November 2022 during the tech downturn and faced a 2025 exchange sanction over a disputed charge, but it remains active.
notes: Company website returned 403, so the site was not read. YC page lists founding year 2019 while its description says 2018. Series B valuation of about 1 billion dollars is reported in a search summary only and is not recorded as post money. The e27 seed article gives no date; January 2019 is inferred from its URL and other reports. The Bareksa source is dated about four months after the batch. Series A split into 25 million in January 2021 and 65 million extension in March 2021 per search summaries and KrASIA; the 65 million figure is from the Jakarta Post search snippet only. Layoffs of 67 staff (8 percent) in November 2022 per Jakarta Post.
